# Order & Inventory System — Specification

You are building a small **order-management backend** with inventory reservation,
customer funds, and order processing. The system is exercised exclusively through
the HTTP API defined here and in `openapi.yaml`. The **acceptance test suite is
the requirement**: your implementation is done when the whole suite passes.

The suite includes concurrency scenarios. They are part of the contract: the
system must behave correctly when many requests arrive at the same time.

## Domain

### Product
A product has a `name`, a `unitPrice` (integer cents), and a `stock` (units on
hand). Stock can be replenished. Stock is **never negative** and is **never
oversold**: units are reserved/consumed at most once.

### Customer
A customer has a `name` and a `balance` (integer cents). Funds can be deposited.
Balance is **never negative** and is **never double-spent**.

### Order
An order references one customer, one product, and a `quantity` (≥ 1).
The **client supplies the order id** (UUID) at creation; creating the same order
id again is **idempotent** — it must not create a second order, charge twice, or
notify twice, regardless of timing or concurrency.

Order lifecycle (asynchronous processing is allowed and expected):

```
PENDING ──> CONFIRMED                       (stock reserved AND amount charged)
       └──> REJECTED(OUT_OF_STOCK)          (insufficient stock; nothing charged)
       └──> REJECTED(INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS)    (stock was reserved, then released; nothing charged)
```

- Order total = `quantity × product.unitPrice` at processing time.
- A CONFIRMED order has: product stock decreased by `quantity` and customer
  balance decreased by the total — both **exactly once**.
- A REJECTED order leaves **no residual effect**: any reservation made during
  processing is released (compensation), and no money is taken.
- Status never regresses (e.g. CONFIRMED never becomes PENDING again).

### Notifications
Every order **decision** (CONFIRMED or REJECTED) produces **exactly one**
notification for the order's customer — never zero, never two — under any
concurrency or retry pattern.

### Statistics
A statistics view reports, across all orders: `confirmed` count, `rejected`
count, and `revenue` (sum of totals of confirmed orders).

## Consistency model

Reads may be **eventually consistent**: after a write, views (order status,
stats, notifications, product/customer views) must **converge within 10
seconds**. The acceptance tests poll with a deadline; they never require
synchronous read-your-writes on views. Conservation must hold at convergence:

- `sum(customer balance decreases) == stats.revenue`
- `initial stock + restocks == remaining stock + sum(quantity of CONFIRMED orders)`

## API summary (normative schema in `openapi.yaml`)

| Method & path | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /products` | Create product `{name, unitPrice, stock}` → `201 {id, ...}` |
| `GET /products/{id}` | → `200 {id, name, unitPrice, stock}` (stock = on hand, minus reserved/confirmed) |
| `POST /products/{id}/restock` | `{units}` adds stock → `202`. Concurrent restocks must ALL be applied. |
| `POST /customers` | Create customer `{name, balance}` → `201 {id, ...}` |
| `GET /customers/{id}` | → `200 {id, name, balance}` |
| `POST /customers/{id}/deposit` | `{amount}` adds funds → `202`. Concurrent deposits must ALL be applied. |
| `POST /orders` | `{orderId, customerId, productId, quantity}` → `202 {orderId, status}`. Idempotent on `orderId`. |
| `GET /orders/{id}` | → `200 {orderId, customerId, productId, quantity, status, reason?, total?}` |
| `GET /customers/{id}/notifications` | → `200 [{orderId, status, ...}]` |
| `GET /stats/orders` | → `200 {confirmed, rejected, revenue}` |

Errors: malformed body → `400`; unknown id on GET/POST-subresource → `404`;
`quantity < 1`, `units < 1`, `amount < 1` → `400`. Unknown `customerId`/
`productId` in `POST /orders` → `400` or order ends `REJECTED` (either accepted).

## Delivery requirements (identical for every implementation)

1. Java 21, Maven, single Spring Boot deployable — start from the provided
   skeleton; do not change its build coordinates or dependency constraints.
2. Root package `com.study.app` with layer sub-packages:
   `web` (HTTP), `command` (write side), `query` (read side / views),
   `domain` (domain model), `config` (wiring). Keep code in its layer.
3. The app must serve HTTP on `${PORT}` (already configured in the skeleton)
   and expose Spring Actuator `/actuator/health` (already configured).
4. Use the provided PostgreSQL (already configured in the skeleton) for any
   persistence you need. Do not add other infrastructure.
5. **Durability (real-world deployment).** All business state — products,
   customers, orders, balances, stock, notifications, statistics — MUST be
   persisted in the provided PostgreSQL. The system MUST recover its state
   after a process restart: stopping and restarting the application (the
   database keeps running) must not lose committed orders, balances, or stock.
   In-memory-only storage (maps, lists, caches as the source of truth) is NOT
   acceptable. This is exercised by a restart-survival check.
6. Definition of done: `mvn -B verify` succeeds, the app boots, and the
   acceptance suite in `./acceptance-tests` passes (`make test`).

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Order & Inventory System
  version: "1.0"
  description: >
    Normative REST contract. Behavior is specified in SPEC.md; the acceptance
    test suite is the requirement. Reads may be eventually consistent with a
    10-second convergence deadline.

paths:
  /products:
    post:
      summary: Create a product
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name, unitPrice, stock]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                unitPrice: { type: integer, minimum: 1, description: cents }
                stock: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Product" }
        "400": { description: Malformed }

  /products/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get product view
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Product" }
        "404": { description: Unknown product }

  /products/{id}/restock:
    post:
      summary: Add stock. Concurrent restocks must all be applied (no lost update).
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [units]
              properties:
                units: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
      responses:
        "202": { description: Accepted }
        "400": { description: Malformed / units < 1 }
        "404": { description: Unknown product }

  /customers:
    post:
      summary: Create a customer
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name, balance]
              properties:
                name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                balance: { type: integer, minimum: 0, description: cents }
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Customer" }
        "400": { description: Malformed }

  /customers/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get customer view
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Customer" }
        "404": { description: Unknown customer }

  /customers/{id}/deposit:
    post:
      summary: Add funds. Concurrent deposits must all be applied (no lost update).
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [amount]
              properties:
                amount: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
      responses:
        "202": { description: Accepted }
        "400": { description: Malformed / amount < 1 }
        "404": { description: Unknown customer }

  /customers/{id}/notifications:
    get:
      summary: Notifications for the customer — exactly one per order decision.
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Notification" }
        "404": { description: Unknown customer }

  /orders:
    post:
      summary: >
        Place an order. Client supplies orderId (UUID); the operation is
        idempotent on orderId under any concurrency — at most one order,
        one charge, one notification. Processing may be asynchronous.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [orderId, customerId, productId, quantity]
              properties:
                orderId: { type: string, format: uuid }
                customerId: { type: string }
                productId: { type: string }
                quantity: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Accepted (also returned for an idempotent replay; 200 acceptable for replays)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Order" }
        "200":
          description: Idempotent replay — current order state
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Order" }
        "400": { description: Malformed / quantity < 1 / unknown references (REJECTED outcome also acceptable) }

  /orders/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get order view. Status never regresses.
      parameters: [{ name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string } }]
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Order" }
        "404": { description: Unknown order (allowed only before the write converges) }

  /stats/orders:
    get:
      summary: Aggregate statistics over all orders.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [confirmed, rejected, revenue]
                properties:
                  confirmed: { type: integer }
                  rejected: { type: integer }
                  revenue: { type: integer, description: sum of totals of confirmed orders, cents }

components:
  schemas:
    Product:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, unitPrice, stock]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        unitPrice: { type: integer }
        stock: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
    Customer:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, balance]
      properties:
        id: { type: string }
        name: { type: string }
        balance: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
    Order:
      type: object
      required: [orderId, customerId, productId, quantity, status]
      properties:
        orderId: { type: string }
        customerId: { type: string }
        productId: { type: string }
        quantity: { type: integer }
        status: { type: string, enum: [PENDING, CONFIRMED, REJECTED] }
        reason: { type: string, enum: [OUT_OF_STOCK, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS], description: present iff REJECTED }
        total: { type: integer, description: present iff CONFIRMED }
    Notification:
      type: object
      required: [orderId, status]
      properties:
        orderId: { type: string }
        status: { type: string, enum: [CONFIRMED, REJECTED] }
        reason: { type: string }

echo "all services READY"

"""Shared fixtures/helpers for the order-inventory acceptance suite.

Black-box HTTP only. Reads may be eventually consistent: ALWAYS assert through
the polling helpers, never via sleep-and-hope.

Environment:
  BASE_URL          target system            (default http://localhost:8080)
  DEADLINE_SECONDS  convergence deadline     (default 10, per SPEC.md)
  RNG_SEED          optional reproducibility seed; unset = random per execution
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import random
import string
import time
import uuid
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import Any, Callable

import httpx
import pytest

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")
DEADLINE = float(os.environ.get("DEADLINE_SECONDS", "10"))
LONG_DEADLINE = 3 * DEADLINE  # for burst convergence (many async decisions)

_seed = os.environ.get("RNG_SEED")
rng = random.Random(int(_seed)) if _seed else random.Random()


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def client() -> httpx.Client:
    with httpx.Client(base_url=BASE_URL, timeout=30.0) as c:
        yield c


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

def rand_name(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}-" + "".join(rng.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))


def new_order_id() -> str:
    return str(uuid.UUID(int=rng.getrandbits(128), version=4))


def wait_until(probe: Callable[[], bool], deadline: float = DEADLINE, what: str = "condition") -> None:
    """Poll `probe` until truthy or the deadline elapses."""
    end = time.monotonic() + deadline
    last_err: Exception | None = None
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        try:
            if probe():
                return
            last_err = None
        except (httpx.HTTPError, AssertionError, KeyError) as e:  # transient view lag
            last_err = e
        time.sleep(0.2)
    pytest.fail(f"timed out after {deadline}s waiting for {what}"
                + (f" (last error: {last_err})" if last_err else ""))


def get_json(client: httpx.Client, path: str) -> Any:
    r = client.get(path)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET {path} -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return r.json()


def read_settled(client: httpx.Client, path: str, deadline: float = DEADLINE) -> Any:
    """GET that tolerates read-after-write lag: polls until the read model has
    materialised (HTTP 200) or the deadline elapses. The read side is eventually
    consistent — reading back a just-written entity may 404 briefly, which is a
    design property, not a fault. Use this for reading freshly-written entities;
    business invariants (conservation, exactly-once) are still asserted strictly
    via wait_until elsewhere."""
    end = time.monotonic() + deadline
    last: httpx.Response | None = None
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        last = client.get(path)
        if last.status_code == 200:
            return last.json()
        time.sleep(0.1)
    assert False, (f"GET {path} not readable within {deadline}s "
                   f"(last {last.status_code if last is not None else 'n/a'})")


def parallel(callables: list[Callable[[], Any]], max_workers: int | None = None) -> list[Any]:
    """Fire callables concurrently; return results in submission order."""
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers or len(callables)) as pool:
        return [f.result() for f in [pool.submit(c) for c in callables]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- factories

def create_product(client: httpx.Client, *, unit_price: int, stock: int) -> str:
    r = client.post("/products", json={"name": rand_name("prod"), "unitPrice": unit_price, "stock": stock})
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST /products -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return str(r.json()["id"])


def create_customer(client: httpx.Client, *, balance: int) -> str:
    r = client.post("/customers", json={"name": rand_name("cust"), "balance": balance})
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST /customers -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return str(r.json()["id"])


def place_order(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str, customer_id: str, product_id: str,
                quantity: int) -> httpx.Response:
    return client.post("/orders", json={
        "orderId": order_id, "customerId": customer_id,
        "productId": product_id, "quantity": quantity,
    })


def order_status(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str) -> dict | None:
    r = client.get(f"/orders/{order_id}")
    if r.status_code == 404:  # allowed only before the write converges
        return None
    assert r.status_code == 200
    return r.json()


def wait_decided(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str, deadline: float = DEADLINE) -> dict:
    """Poll until the order leaves PENDING; return the decided view."""
    result: dict = {}

    def probe() -> bool:
        o = order_status(client, order_id)
        if o and o["status"] in ("CONFIRMED", "REJECTED", "CANCELLED"):
            result.update(o)
            return True
        return False

    wait_until(probe, deadline, what=f"order {order_id} decision")
    return result


def wait_all_decided(client: httpx.Client, order_ids: list[str],
                     deadline: float = LONG_DEADLINE) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Wait for a burst of orders to all reach a decision."""
    decided: dict[str, dict] = {}

    def probe() -> bool:
        for oid in order_ids:
            if oid in decided:
                continue
            o = order_status(client, oid)
            if o and o["status"] in ("CONFIRMED", "REJECTED", "CANCELLED"):
                decided[oid] = o
        return len(decided) == len(order_ids)

    wait_until(probe, deadline, what=f"{len(order_ids)} order decisions")
    return decided


def notifications_for(client: httpx.Client, customer_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    return get_json(client, f"/customers/{customer_id}/notifications")


def stats(client: httpx.Client) -> dict:
    return get_json(client, "/stats/orders")

"""Order lifecycle: confirmation, rejection paths, compensation, notifications, stats."""

from conftest import (
    create_customer,
    create_product,
    get_json,
    new_order_id,
    notifications_for,
    place_order,
    stats,
    wait_decided,
    wait_until,
)


def test_happy_path_confirmed(client):
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=300, stock=10)
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=5_000)
    oid = new_order_id()

    r = place_order(client, oid, cid, pid, quantity=2)
    assert r.status_code in (200, 202), r.text[:200]

    o = wait_decided(client, oid)
    assert o["status"] == "CONFIRMED", o
    assert o.get("total") == 600

    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/products/{pid}")["stock"] == 8,
               what="stock decremented exactly once")
    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/customers/{cid}")["balance"] == 4_400,
               what="balance charged exactly once")
    wait_until(lambda: any(n["orderId"] == oid and n["status"] == "CONFIRMED"
                           for n in notifications_for(client, cid)),
               what="confirmation notification")


def test_out_of_stock_rejected_nothing_charged(client):
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=300, stock=1)
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=5_000)
    oid = new_order_id()

    place_order(client, oid, cid, pid, quantity=5)
    o = wait_decided(client, oid)
    assert o["status"] == "REJECTED", o
    assert o.get("reason") == "OUT_OF_STOCK", o

    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/products/{pid}")["stock"] == 1,
               what="stock untouched")
    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/customers/{cid}")["balance"] == 5_000,
               what="nothing charged")


def test_insufficient_funds_rejected_with_compensation(client):
    """The saga path: stock may be reserved first, then must be RELEASED."""
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=1_000, stock=4)
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=500)   # cannot afford even one unit
    oid = new_order_id()

    place_order(client, oid, cid, pid, quantity=1)
    o = wait_decided(client, oid)
    assert o["status"] == "REJECTED", o
    assert o.get("reason") == "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", o

    # compensation: any transient reservation is released; no residual effect
    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/products/{pid}")["stock"] == 4,
               what="reservation released (compensation)")
    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/customers/{cid}")["balance"] == 500,
               what="no money taken")
    wait_until(lambda: any(n["orderId"] == oid and n["status"] == "REJECTED"
                           for n in notifications_for(client, cid)),
               what="rejection notification")


def test_stats_reflect_decisions(client):

"""Shared fixtures/helpers for the order-inventory acceptance suite.

Black-box HTTP only. Reads may be eventually consistent: ALWAYS assert through
the polling helpers, never via sleep-and-hope.

Environment:
  BASE_URL          target system            (default http://localhost:8080)
  DEADLINE_SECONDS  convergence deadline     (default 10, per SPEC.md)
  RNG_SEED          optional reproducibility seed; unset = random per execution
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import random
import string
import time
import uuid
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import Any, Callable

import httpx
import pytest

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")
DEADLINE = float(os.environ.get("DEADLINE_SECONDS", "10"))
LONG_DEADLINE = 3 * DEADLINE  # for burst convergence (many async decisions)

_seed = os.environ.get("RNG_SEED")
rng = random.Random(int(_seed)) if _seed else random.Random()


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def client() -> httpx.Client:
    with httpx.Client(base_url=BASE_URL, timeout=30.0) as c:
        yield c


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

def rand_name(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}-" + "".join(rng.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))


def new_order_id() -> str:
    return str(uuid.UUID(int=rng.getrandbits(128), version=4))


def wait_until(probe: Callable[[], bool], deadline: float = DEADLINE, what: str = "condition") -> None:
    """Poll `probe` until truthy or the deadline elapses."""
    end = time.monotonic() + deadline
    last_err: Exception | None = None
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        try:
            if probe():
                return
            last_err = None
        except (httpx.HTTPError, AssertionError, KeyError) as e:  # transient view lag
            last_err = e
        time.sleep(0.2)
    pytest.fail(f"timed out after {deadline}s waiting for {what}"
                + (f" (last error: {last_err})" if last_err else ""))


def get_json(client: httpx.Client, path: str) -> Any:
    r = client.get(path)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET {path} -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return r.json()


def read_settled(client: httpx.Client, path: str, deadline: float = DEADLINE) -> Any:
    """GET that tolerates read-after-write lag: polls until the read model has
    materialised (HTTP 200) or the deadline elapses. The read side is eventually
    consistent — reading back a just-written entity may 404 briefly, which is a
    design property, not a fault. Use this for reading freshly-written entities;
    business invariants (conservation, exactly-once) are still asserted strictly
    via wait_until elsewhere."""
    end = time.monotonic() + deadline
    last: httpx.Response | None = None
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        last = client.get(path)
        if last.status_code == 200:
            return last.json()
        time.sleep(0.1)
    assert False, (f"GET {path} not readable within {deadline}s "
                   f"(last {last.status_code if last is not None else 'n/a'})")


def parallel(callables: list[Callable[[], Any]], max_workers: int | None = None) -> list[Any]:
    """Fire callables concurrently; return results in submission order."""
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers or len(callables)) as pool:
        return [f.result() for f in [pool.submit(c) for c in callables]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- factories

def create_product(client: httpx.Client, *, unit_price: int, stock: int) -> str:
    r = client.post("/products", json={"name": rand_name("prod"), "unitPrice": unit_price, "stock": stock})
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST /products -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return str(r.json()["id"])


def create_customer(client: httpx.Client, *, balance: int) -> str:
    r = client.post("/customers", json={"name": rand_name("cust"), "balance": balance})
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST /customers -> {r.status_code}: {r.text[:200]}"
    return str(r.json()["id"])


def place_order(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str, customer_id: str, product_id: str,
                quantity: int) -> httpx.Response:
    return client.post("/orders", json={
        "orderId": order_id, "customerId": customer_id,
        "productId": product_id, "quantity": quantity,
    })


def order_status(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str) -> dict | None:
    r = client.get(f"/orders/{order_id}")
    if r.status_code == 404:  # allowed only before the write converges
        return None
    assert r.status_code == 200
    return r.json()


def wait_decided(client: httpx.Client, order_id: str, deadline: float = DEADLINE) -> dict:
    """Poll until the order leaves PENDING; return the decided view."""
    result: dict = {}

    def probe() -> bool:
        o = order_status(client, order_id)
        if o and o["status"] in ("CONFIRMED", "REJECTED", "CANCELLED"):
            result.update(o)
            return True
        return False

    wait_until(probe, deadline, what=f"order {order_id} decision")
    return result


def wait_all_decided(client: httpx.Client, order_ids: list[str],
                     deadline: float = LONG_DEADLINE) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Wait for a burst of orders to all reach a decision."""
    decided: dict[str, dict] = {}

    def probe() -> bool:
        for oid in order_ids:
            if oid in decided:
                continue
            o = order_status(client, oid)
            if o and o["status"] in ("CONFIRMED", "REJECTED", "CANCELLED"):
                decided[oid] = o
        return len(decided) == len(order_ids)

    wait_until(probe, deadline, what=f"{len(order_ids)} order decisions")
    return decided


def notifications_for(client: httpx.Client, customer_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    return get_json(client, f"/customers/{customer_id}/notifications")


def stats(client: httpx.Client) -> dict:
    return get_json(client, "/stats/orders")

    funds: exactly one confirmed, balance ends 0, never negative."""
    n = 6
    price = 900
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=price, stock=100)  # stock NOT the constraint
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=price)               # affords exactly one

    oids = [new_order_id() for _ in range(n)]
    parallel([(lambda o=o: place_order(client, o, cid, pid, quantity=1)) for o in oids])

    decided = wait_all_decided(client, oids)
    confirmed = [o for o in decided.values() if o["status"] == "CONFIRMED"]
    rejected = [o for o in decided.values() if o["status"] == "REJECTED"]

    assert len(confirmed) == 1, f"double spend: {len(confirmed)} orders confirmed"
    assert len(rejected) == n - 1
    assert all(o.get("reason") == "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS" for o in rejected)

    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/customers/{cid}")["balance"] == 0,
               what="balance exactly spent")
    # compensation: every losing order released its reservation
    wait_until(lambda: get_json(client, f"/products/{pid}")["stock"] == 99,
               what="exactly one unit sold; all losing reservations released")


def test_exactly_once_notifications_under_load(client):
    """A burst of B orders (mixed outcomes): exactly one notification per
    decision — never zero, never two — under concurrent processing."""
    b = 20
    price = 150
    affordable = rng.randint(8, 12)
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=price, stock=b * 2)
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=affordable * price)  # only some succeed

    oids = [new_order_id() for _ in range(b)]
    parallel([(lambda o=o: place_order(client, o, cid, pid, quantity=1)) for o in oids])
    decided = wait_all_decided(client, oids)
    assert len(decided) == b

    def exactly_one_each() -> bool:
        ns = notifications_for(client, cid)
        counts = {oid: 0 for oid in oids}
        for nt in ns:
            if nt["orderId"] in counts:
                counts[nt["orderId"]] += 1
        assert all(c <= 1 for c in counts.values()), f"duplicate notifications: {counts}"
        return all(c == 1 for c in counts.values())

    wait_until(exactly_one_each, deadline=LONG_DEADLINE,
               what="exactly one notification per decided order")


def test_status_never_regresses_and_conservation(client):
    """Causal ordering + conservation under a mixed burst:
    - an order observed CONFIRMED/REJECTED never goes back to PENDING,
    - confirmed+rejected deltas equal the burst size,
    - revenue delta == sum of confirmed totals == customer balance decrease."""
    before = stats(client)
    b = 15
    price = 200
    pid = create_product(client, unit_price=price, stock=rng.randint(5, 9))
    start_balance = b * price * 2
    cid = create_customer(client, balance=start_balance)

    oids = [new_order_id() for _ in range(b)]
    parallel([(lambda o=o: place_order(client, o, cid, pid, quantity=1)) for o in oids])

    # sample statuses while processing: any decided order must stay decided
    seen_decided: dict[str, str] = {}
    import time
    end = time.monotonic() + DEADLINE
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        for oid in oids:
            r = client.get(f"/orders/{oid}")
            if r.status_code != 200:
                continue
            st = r.json()["status"]
            if oid in seen_decided:
                assert st == seen_decided[oid], \
                    f"status regression on {oid}: {seen_decided[oid]} -> {st}"
            elif st in ("CONFIRMED", "REJECTED"):
                seen_decided[oid] = st
        if len(seen_decided) == b:
            break
        time.sleep(0.15)

    decided = wait_all_decided(client, oids)
    n_confirmed = sum(1 for o in decided.values() if o["status"] == "CONFIRMED")
    n_rejected = b - n_confirmed
    revenue_expected = n_confirmed * price

    def conserved() -> bool:
        s = stats(client)
        balance = get_json(client, f"/customers/{cid}")["balance"]
        return (s["confirmed"] - before["confirmed"] == n_confirmed
                and s["rejected"] - before["rejected"] == n_rejected
                and s["revenue"] - before["revenue"] == revenue_expected
                and start_balance - balance == revenue_expected)

    wait_until(conserved, deadline=LONG_DEADLINE,
               what="conservation: stats == money moved == stock sold")

1	# Evento Framework — Developer Guide (v2.1.0)
2	
3	Evento is a JVM (Java 17+) framework for building event-driven, CQRS / event-sourced
4	applications structured by the **RECQ component pattern**. A *bundle* is one deployable
5	unit (a Spring Boot app, in the integration pattern) that registers components; bundles
6	talk to an **Evento Server** (the message bus / event store) over a TCP transport.
7	Components never call each other directly — they exchange **messages** (commands,
8	events, queries) through gateways, and the platform routes them.
9	
10	All annotations live under `com.evento.common.modeling.annotations`; payload base
11	classes under `com.evento.common.modeling.messaging.payload`; query response wrappers
12	under `com.evento.common.modeling.messaging.query`; state base classes under
13	`com.evento.common.modeling.state`; gateways under `com.evento.common.messaging.gateway`.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. Core concepts
18	
19	### The seven RECQ component roles
20	
21	A component is a class annotated with exactly one of the role annotations below. It is
22	discovered by classpath scanning under the bundle base package and instantiated through
23	the configured injector (Spring `BeanFactory::getBean` in the integration pattern).
24	
25	| Role | Annotation | Side | Holds state? | May emit | Handler annotation(s) |
26	|------|-----------|------|--------------|----------|-----------------------|
27	| **Invoker** | `@Invoker` | edge | no | commands + queries (via gateways) | `@InvocationHandler` |
28	| **Aggregate** | `@Aggregate` | command | yes (event-sourced `AggregateState`) | exactly one `DomainEvent` per command | `@AggregateCommandHandler`, `@EventSourcingHandler` |
29	| **Service** | `@Service` | command | no | exactly one `ServiceEvent` per command (may also send commands / query) | `@CommandHandler` |
30	| **Projector** | `@Projector` | query | writes a read model | nothing (void handlers) | `@EventHandler` |
31	| **Projection** | `@Projection` | query | reads a read model | query results | `@EventHandler`*, `@QueryHandler` |
32	| **Saga** | `@Saga` | reactive | yes (`SagaState`, persisted) | commands + queries | `@SagaEventHandler` |
33	| **Observer** | `@Observer` | reactive | no | commands + queries | `@EventHandler` |
34	
35	\* A `@Projection` may also carry `@EventHandler` methods, but the canonical split in the
36	reference apps is: **Projector writes** the read model, **Projection reads/queries** it.
37	
38	What each may / may not do:
39	
40	- **Invoker** — the *only* place outside reactive components that may originate commands
41	  and queries. It is the bridge from the outside world (HTTP, CLI) into the bus. It holds
42	  no domain state and emits no events. Gateways are available only inside its
43	  `@InvocationHandler` methods (see §3).
44	- **Aggregate** — the consistency boundary. A command handler validates against the
45	  current `AggregateState` and returns **one** `DomainEvent`. It must **not** call
46	  gateways to mutate other aggregates. State is rebuilt by replaying events through
47	  `@EventSourcingHandler` methods (event sourcing); there is no setter-driven state.
48	- **Service** — stateless command handling for logic that is not a single
49	  event-sourced aggregate (integrations, cross-cutting commands). Returns one
50	  `ServiceEvent`. May itself send commands / queries via injected gateways.
51	- **Projector** — consumes events and updates a read model (DB table, store). Idempotent,
52	  retryable, returns `void`. One projector instance is the single active consumer for its
53	  events (see §3).
54	- **Projection** — answers queries by reading the read model the projector built.
55	- **Saga** — a long-running, stateful coordinator. Each `@SagaEventHandler` returns the
56	  updated `SagaState`; events are correlated to a saga instance by an
57	  *association property* (see §2). Used to orchestrate multi-step / multi-aggregate
58	  workflows by reacting to events and sending follow-up commands.
59	- **Observer** — stateless reaction to events (notifications, side effects). May send
60	  commands but keeps no state and does no correlation.
61	
62	### Command side vs query side
63	
64	- **Command side**: Invoker → `CommandGateway.send(cmd)` → Aggregate/Service command
65	  handler → produces an event → event is appended to the store and published.
66	- **Query side**: events are consumed asynchronously by Projectors that build read
67	  models; Invoker → `QueryGateway.query(q)` → Projection query handler reads the model.
68	
69	The read side is **eventually consistent**: after a command's future completes, the
70	event has been stored, but projectors may not yet have applied it.
71	
72	### Events are the only state-change vehicle
73	
74	Aggregate/Service command handlers do not mutate state directly; they **return an
75	event**. Aggregate state changes only by applying events in `@EventSourcingHandler`.
76	Read models change only inside projector `@EventHandler`s reacting to events. There is no
77	other sanctioned way to change persistent state.
78	
79	### One event per command
80	
81	A command handler (`@AggregateCommandHandler` / `@CommandHandler`) returns a **single**
82	event object — its return type is one `DomainEvent` (aggregate) or one `ServiceEvent`
83	(service), never a collection. To model an operation with several effects:
84	
85	1. **Richer / composite event** — emit one event that carries all the data, and let
86	   multiple `@EventHandler`s (in one or more projectors/observers) react to it. This is
87	   the preferred approach.
88	2. **Saga / Observer delegation** — emit the one event, then have a Saga or Observer
89	   react to it and `send` additional commands, each of which produces its own event.
90	   This decomposes a multi-aggregate operation into a chain of single-event commands.
91	
92	A command handler may also `throw` to reject the command (see §5).
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 2. Annotations & handler signatures (verified)
97	
98	### Component annotations
99	
100	```java
101	@Aggregate(snapshotFrequency = 5)   // int snapshotFrequency() default -1; -1 = no snapshots
102	@Projector(version = 1)             // int version()  — REQUIRED, no default
103	@Projection                         // no attributes
104	@Saga(version = 1)                  // int version()  — REQUIRED, no default
105	@Service                            // no attributes
106	@Observer(version = 1)              // int version()  — REQUIRED, no default
107	@Invoker                            // no attributes
108	```
109	
110	> The javadoc examples in the source show `context = {...}` on `@Projector`/`@Saga`/
111	> `@Observer`, but in v2.1.0 those annotations declare **only `version()`** — there is no
112	> `context` attribute. Per-component contexts are set on the builder instead via
113	> `Builder.setComponentContexts(Class<?>, String...)`. Do **not** put `context=` in the
114	> annotation; it will not compile.
115	
116	All component annotations are `@Target(TYPE) @Retention(RUNTIME)` and meta-annotated
117	`@Component`.
118	
119	### Handler annotations
120	
121	```java
122	// On @Aggregate methods:
123	@AggregateCommandHandler(init = false)   // boolean init() default false; init=true => creation handler
124	@EventSourcingHandler                    // no attributes
125	
126	// On @Service methods:
127	@CommandHandler                          // no attributes
128	
129	// On @Projector / @Projection / @Observer methods:
130	@EventHandler(retry = -1, retryDelay = 1000)  // int retry() default -1; int retryDelay() default 1000 (ms)
131	
132	// On @Projection methods:
133	@QueryHandler                            // no attributes
134	
135	// On @Saga methods:
136	@SagaEventHandler(init = false, associationProperty = "orderId", retry = -1, retryDelay = 1000)
137	//   boolean init() default false; String associationProperty() (REQUIRED); int retry()/retryDelay()
138	
139	// On @Invoker methods:
140	@InvocationHandler                       // no attributes
141	```
142	
143	All handler annotations are `@Target(METHOD) @Retention(RUNTIME)` and meta-annotated
144	`@Handler`.
145	
146	### Handler method parameter injection
147	
148	Handler methods are invoked by reflection; the framework resolves each parameter **by
149	type**. You declare only the parameters you need, in any order:
150	
151	- The **payload** (the command / event / query object) — always present.
152	- The matching **state** object (`AggregateState` subclass for aggregates, `SagaState`
153	  subclass for sagas) — for aggregate command/sourcing handlers and saga event handlers.
154	- `CommandGateway` and/or `QueryGateway` — injected into Service `@CommandHandler`,
155	  Saga `@SagaEventHandler`, and Observer `@EventHandler` methods that declare them.
156	  (Inside an Invoker, gateways come from `getCommandGateway()`/`getQueryGateway()`, see §3.)
157	- `Metadata` — optional.
158	
159	### Payload base classes & conventions
160	
161	```java
162	// Commands (sent via CommandGateway)
163	abstract class Command extends TrackablePayload {
164	    public abstract String getAggregateId();   // routing / consistency key
165	    public abstract String getLockId();
166	}
167	abstract class DomainCommand extends Command { // targets an Aggregate
168	    // getLockId() returns getAggregateId() by default; you implement getAggregateId()
169	}
170	abstract class ServiceCommand extends Command { // targets a Service
171	    public String getLockId()      { return null; }      // override to set a lock key
172	    public String getAggregateId() { return getLockId(); }
173	}
174	
175	// Events (returned by command handlers; never constructed by callers)
176	abstract class Event extends TrackablePayload {
177	    public String getContext();
178	    public <T extends Event> T setContext(String);   // default Context.DEFAULT
179	}
180	abstract class DomainEvent  extends Event {}  // returned by @AggregateCommandHandler
181	abstract class ServiceEvent extends Event {}  // returned by @CommandHandler (Service)
182	
183	// Queries
184	abstract class Query<T extends QueryResponse<?>> extends TrackablePayload {
185	    public Class<T> getResponseType();  // derived from the generic param, do not override
186	}
187	
188	// Views & query responses
189	interface View extends Payload {}                       // your read DTOs implement this
190	class Single<T extends View>   extends QueryResponse<T>  // Single.of(view)
191	class Multiple<T extends View> extends QueryResponse<T>  // Multiple.of(collection) / of(varargs)
192	
193	// State
194	abstract class AggregateState implements Serializable { boolean isDeleted(); void setDeleted(boolean); }
195	abstract class SagaState      implements Serializable {
196	    boolean isEnded(); void setEnded(boolean);
197	    void setAssociation(String field, String value);
198	    String getAssociation(String field);
199	    Map<String,String> getAssociations();
200	}
201	```
202	
203	Conventions:
204	- **Aggregate id** is whatever `DomainCommand.getAggregateId()` returns — you implement it
205	  to return your business key (e.g. `return orderId;`). Events are correlated to the same
206	  aggregate because their handlers read the id from the event fields you set.
207	- A `DomainCommand` with `init=true` handler **creates** the aggregate; a non-init handler
208	  requires the aggregate to already exist (else `AggregateNotInitializedError`); an init
209	  handler on an existing aggregate throws `AggregateInitializedError`.
210	- Payloads must be JSON-serializable POJOs: **public no-arg constructor + getters/setters**
211	  for every field. (Jackson is used; missing no-arg ctor or fields => serialization failure.)
212	- `Query<Single<OrderView>>` ⇒ its `@QueryHandler` must return `Single<OrderView>`.
213	  `Query<Multiple<OrderView>>` ⇒ returns `Multiple<OrderView>`.
214	
215	### Gateways
216	
217	```java
218	package com.evento.common.messaging.gateway;
219	
220	interface CommandGateway extends Gateway {
221	    <R> CompletableFuture<R> send(Command command);
222	    <R> CompletableFuture<R> send(Command command, long timeout, TimeUnit unit);
223	    <R> CompletableFuture<R> send(Command command, Metadata metadata);
224	    // ... overloads with Metadata / handledMessage / timeout
225	}
226	
227	interface QueryGateway extends Gateway {
228	    <T extends QueryResponse<?>> CompletableFuture<T> query(Query<T> query);
229	    <T extends QueryResponse<?>> CompletableFuture<T> query(Query<T> query, long timeout, TimeUnit unit);
230	    // ... overloads with Metadata
231	}
232	```
233	
234	> **There is NO `sendAndWait` in v2.** `send(...)` and `query(...)` are **asynchronous**
235	> and return `CompletableFuture`. To block, call `.get()` (throws checked
236	> `ExecutionException` / `InterruptedException`) or `.join()`.
237	> `send(...)` resolves to the event the handler produced (or, in practice, you often
238	> ignore the result). `query(...)` resolves to the `QueryResponse` (`Single`/`Multiple`);
239	> call `.getData()` on it.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## 3. Wiring & runtime
244	
245	### Bootstrap — `EventoBundle.Builder`
246	
247	The skeleton ships this pre-wired bean (**do not modify it**; mirror it exactly):
248	
249	```java
250	package com.study.app.config;
251	
252	import com.evento.application.EventoBundle;
253	import com.evento.application.bus.ClusterNodeAddress;
254	import com.evento.application.bus.EventoServerMessageBusConfiguration;
255	import com.study.app.App;
256	import org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanFactory;
257	import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
258	import org.springframework.beans.factory.config.ConfigurableBeanFactory;
259	import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
260	import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
261	import org.springframework.context.annotation.Scope;
262	
263	@Configuration
264	public class EventoConfiguration {
265	
266	    @Bean
267	    @Scope(ConfigurableBeanFactory.SCOPE_SINGLETON)
268	    public EventoBundle eventoApplication(
269	            @Value("${evento.server.host}") String host,
270	            @Value("${evento.server.port}") int port,
271	            @Value("${evento.bundle.id}") String bundleId,
272	            @Value("${evento.bundle.version}") long version,
273	            BeanFactory factory) throws Exception {
274	        return EventoBundle.Builder.builder()
275	                .setBasePackage(App.class.getPackage())
276	                .setBundleId(bundleId)
277	                .setBundleVersion(version)
278	                .setEventoServerMessageBusConfiguration(new EventoServerMessageBusConfiguration(
279	                        new ClusterNodeAddress(host, port)))
280	                .setInjector(factory::getBean)
281	                .start();
282	    }
283	}
284	```
285	
286	Key builder methods (all return `Builder`; `start()` returns `EventoBundle`):
287	`setBasePackage(Package)`, `setBundleId(String)`, `setBundleVersion(long)`,
288	`setEventoServerMessageBusConfiguration(...)`, `setInjector(Function<Class<?>,Object>)`,
289	`setComponentContexts(Class<?>, String...)`,
290	`setConsumerEngineConfigBuilder(BiFunction<EventoServer,PerformanceService,ConsumerEngineConfig>)`,
291	`setStrictConfinement(boolean)`. Components annotated with the role annotations under the
292	base package are discovered and registered automatically; `setInjector(factory::getBean)`
293	means each component is obtained from the Spring context (so you may inject Spring beans
294	into component constructors).
295	
296	`@SpringBootApplication public class App` is the base package anchor; components live
297	under `com.study.app.*`.
298	
299	### The Invoker pattern (verified)
300	
301	An Invoker is a class annotated `@Invoker` that **extends `InvokerWrapper`**:
302	
303	```java
304	package com.evento.application.proxy;
305	public class InvokerWrapper {
306	    protected CommandGateway getCommandGateway(); // valid only inside @InvocationHandler
307	    protected QueryGateway  getQueryGateway();    // valid only inside @InvocationHandler
308	}
309	```
310	
311	You obtain a usable instance from the bundle with `eventoBundle.getInvoker(MyInvoker.class)`.
312	That returns a proxy: inside methods annotated `@InvocationHandler`, the protected
313	`getCommandGateway()` / `getQueryGateway()` accessors return live, telemetry-wrapped
314	gateways. Called **outside** an `@InvocationHandler` (or on a non-proxied instance) they
315	throw `RuntimeException("getCommandGateway() called outside an @InvocationHandler scope.")`.
316	
317	A Spring REST controller bridges HTTP to the bus by **delegating to an Invoker** obtained
318	from the bundle. The verified, idiomatic shape (see EXAMPLE.md for the full version):
319	
320	```java
321	@RestController
322	public class OrderController {
323	    private final OrderInvoker invoker;   // an @Invoker extending InvokerWrapper
324	    OrderController(EventoBundle bundle) {
325	        this.invoker = bundle.getInvoker(OrderInvoker.class);
326	    }
327	    @PostMapping("/orders")
328	    public String create(@RequestBody CreateOrderRequest r) throws Exception {
329	        return invoker.createOrder(r.orderId(), r.description(), r.quantity());
330	    }
331	}
332	```
333	
334	The controller itself holds no gateway; all command/query origination happens inside the
335	Invoker's `@InvocationHandler` methods, which is what keeps gateway calls *confined* to
336	components (see §5). Each invocation method blocks on the future (`.get()`) to turn the
337	async result into an HTTP response.
338	
339	### Consumer state store / engine options
340	
341	Consumers (Projectors, Sagas, Observers) run on the v2 consumer engine, configured by
342	`setConsumerEngineConfigBuilder(...)`. The default (if unset) is **in-memory**:
343	
344	```java
345	.setConsumerEngineConfigBuilder(ConsumerEngineConfig::inMemory)  // demos/tests
346	```
347	
348	`ConsumerEngineConfig` is a record bundling a `ConsumerProcessor`, a `ConsumerStateStore`
349	(checkpoint / `isEnabled` probe), and a `DeadEventQueue` (DLQ). `inMemory(...)` wires
350	in-memory implementations and is for demos/tests only.
351	
352	**This skeleton is pre-wired for DURABLE persistence** (do not change it): the
353	`EventoConfiguration` builds the consumer engine from the JDBC consumer state store
354	(`com.evento.consumer.state.store.jdbc.*`) backed by the provided PostgreSQL —
355	`JdbcConsumerLock`, `JdbcConsumerStateStore`, `JdbcSagaStateStore`, `JdbcDeadEventQueue`,
356	`JdbcDedupeStore`. As of v2.1.1 the JDBC consumer state store **auto-creates** the
357	`evento_v2_*` tables on first connection (default — no manual Flyway step required; own
358	history table, no clash with your schema).
359	So consumer checkpoints, saga state, the DLQ, and observer dedup all **survive a
360	restart**. You never touch this wiring; just build your aggregates/projectors/sagas and
361	persist any read-model state you add in Postgres too (not in memory).
362	
363	### Exactly-once / ordering semantics the platform provides
364	
365	- **Single active consumer per context** — for a given consumer (identified by component
366	  name + version + context), exactly one instance is active at a time (enforced by the
367	  consumer *lock*). Bump `version` on a Projector/Saga/Observer to force a replay from the
368	  start under a new consumer identity.
369	- **Ordered consumption** — events are delivered to a consumer in event-store sequence
370	  order; the `ConsumerStateStore` checkpoints progress so a restart resumes where it left.
371	- **Dedupe** — a dedupe store guards against re-processing the same event (at-least-once
372	  delivery + dedupe ⇒ effectively-once for idempotent handlers). Make `@EventHandler`s
373	  idempotent regardless.
374	- **Retry** — `@EventHandler` / `@SagaEventHandler` support `retry` / `retryDelay`; after
375	  retries are exhausted the event goes to the **dead-event queue**.
376	
377	---
378	
379	## 4. A worked mini-flow
380	
381	Command → event → projector → projection → query round trip (full code in EXAMPLE.md):
382	
383	1. HTTP `POST /orders` hits `OrderController`, which calls `OrderInvoker.createOrder(...)`.
384	2. Inside the `@InvocationHandler`, `getCommandGateway().send(new CreateOrderCommand(id, desc, qty)).get()`.
385	3. `OrderAggregate.handle(CreateOrderCommand, OrderAggregateState)` (an `init=true`
386	   `@AggregateCommandHandler`) validates and **returns** `new OrderCreatedEvent(id, desc, qty)`.
387	4. The framework stores the event; `@EventSourcingHandler on(OrderCreatedEvent, state)`
388	   rebuilds aggregate state for next time.
389	5. Asynchronously, `OrderProjector.on(OrderCreatedEvent)` (`@EventHandler`) writes an
390	   `OrderView` into the read store.
391	6. HTTP `GET /orders/{id}` → `OrderInvoker.findOrder(id)` →
392	   `getQueryGateway().query(new FindOrderByIdQuery(id)).get().getData()` →
393	   `OrderProjection.query(FindOrderByIdQuery)` (`@QueryHandler`) returns
394	   `Single.of(view)`.
395	
396	Because step 5 is asynchronous, a `GET` issued immediately after the `POST` future
397	resolves may not yet see the view (eventual consistency).
398	
399	---
400	
401	## 5. Common pitfalls
402	
403	- **One event per command.** A command handler returns one event object, not a list. Use
404	  a composite event or saga/observer delegation for multi-effect operations (§1).
405	- **No `sendAndWait`.** Use `send(...)`/`query(...)` and `.get()`/`.join()`. `.get()`
406	  throws checked exceptions — declare `throws Exception` on handler/invoker methods.
407	- **Gateways are confined to components.** Command/Query gateway calls must live inside a
408	  component class (Invoker `@InvocationHandler`, Service `@CommandHandler`, Saga
409	  `@SagaEventHandler`, Observer `@EventHandler`). A gateway call in a plain helper /
410	  injected collaborator / utility is invisible to the framework's static interaction
411	  analysis. The **`ConfinementScanner`** sweeps non-component classes at startup and
412	  **logs a warning** for each such call site; with `setStrictConfinement(true)` startup
413	  **fails** instead. Keep gateway calls in component methods.
414	- **Aggregate state only via event sourcing.** Never store mutable domain state in
415	  aggregate fields and never mutate from a command handler. Command handler reads the
416	  injected `AggregateState` (which may be `null` before the first event — handle it in
417	  the init handler), decides, returns an event; `@EventSourcingHandler` applies it. The
418	  state class must extend `AggregateState`; sourcing handlers may return the (possibly
419	  new) state or mutate it in place and return `void`.
420	- **Rejections / errors propagate to the sender.** Throwing inside a command handler
421	  surfaces as a failed `CompletableFuture` at the caller — `.get()` raises
422	  `ExecutionException` whose cause is your exception (e.g. `IllegalArgumentException`,
423	  `NoSuchElementException`, or framework errors like `AggregateNotInitializedError`).
424	  Validate in the handler and throw to reject.
425	- **Projections lag (eventual consistency).** Do not assume a read model reflects a
426	  just-sent command. The command future completing means *the event is stored*, not *the
427	  projector has applied it*.
428	- **Sagas associate events by property.** Each `@SagaEventHandler` declares
429	  `associationProperty="<field>"`; the framework reads that field from the incoming event
430	  to find the saga instance. The `init=true` handler creates the instance and must call
431	  `state.setAssociation("<field>", value)` so subsequent events correlate. A handler with
432	  no meaningful correlation (e.g. a standalone init) still needs a non-null
433	  `associationProperty` string. Return the updated `SagaState`; call `state.setEnded(true)`
434	  to finish the saga.
435	- **Virtual threads / async.** Observers (and consumers generally) run on virtual-thread
436	  executors. Handlers may block on gateway futures (`.get()`); keep them idempotent and
437	  avoid sharing non-thread-safe mutable state across handler invocations.
438	- **`@Projector`/`@Saga`/`@Observer` require `version`.** It has no default; omitting it
439	  is a compile error. There is no `context` attribute on these annotations in v2.1.0.
440	- **No `@Autowired` on component fields.** The framework rejects field injection at
441	  startup; inject via the component **constructor** (the injector resolves Spring beans).
442	  Wrong: `@Autowired private Repo repo;` — Right: `MyProjector(Repo repo) { this.repo = repo; }`.
443	- **Payload POJOs need no-arg ctor + accessors** for Jackson (de)serialization.
444

# Evento — Multi-Bundle (microservices) wiring

When the task asks for independent services, deliver **four Evento bundles** in
the provided Maven reactor: `edge`, `orders`, `inventory`, `customers`. Each is
its own Spring Boot app with its own `EventoConfiguration` (pre-wired) connecting
to the **same Evento server** — the server is the integration fabric.

Key points (verified against the framework's `evento-lab-microservices`):

- **Shared payloads live in the `api` module.** Put every command/event/query/
  view there; each service depends on `api`. A command defined in `api` can be
  *sent* from one bundle and *handled* in another — the server routes it.
- **Each bundle scans only its own package tree** (`setBasePackage` is pre-wired
  to that module). So place a component in the service that owns it:
  - `orders`: the order `@Aggregate`, the reserve→charge→confirm `@Saga`, the
    stats `@Projector`/`@Projection`.
  - `inventory`: product/stock `@Aggregate` (+ its projection).
  - `customers`: balance `@Aggregate` and the notifications `@Projector`.
  - `edge`: only `@Invoker` + a `@RestController` that calls
    `eventoBundle.getInvoker(...)`; it holds NO aggregates and NO database.

  server to whichever bundle subscribes. You do NOT write HTTP calls between
  services — the broker carries commands/events/queries.

  consumption per consumer; single-active consumption per context; replayable
  event log (a restarted consumer rebuilds its read model). You do not hand-roll
  idempotency, retries, or saga checkpoints — model them as RECQ components.

  (`orders`/`inventory`/`customers`) uses the **JDBC consumer state store**

  dead-letter queue and observer dedup all survive a restart (Flyway creates

  add must likewise be persisted in that service's Postgres, not in memory.
  `edge` is stateless (Invoker only) — no database, no consumer store.

verbatim — micro just distributes the same components across four bundles.

## Summary

I implemented the Order & Inventory system as **four independent Evento bundles** sharing one Evento server, each with its own PostgreSQL database. Services integrate **only** through the server (commands/events/queries) — no service reads another's DB.

### Decomposition (RECQ components)

**`api` module** — shared payloads only: 10 commands, 12 events, 5 queries, 5 views (all extend the Evento base types).

**`inventory`** — owns stock. `ProductAggregate` (`@Aggregate`) is the consistency boundary for stock: reserve emits `StockReservedEvent` or `StockReservationFailedEvent`, release compensates. `ProductProjector`/`ProductProjection` serve the product view from Postgres.

**`customers`** — owns funds. `CustomerAggregate` enforces non-negative, never-double-spent balance: charge emits `ChargedEvent` or `ChargeFailedEvent`. `CustomerProjector`/`Projection` serve the balance view; `NotificationProjector`/`Projection` produce exactly one notification per decision (keyed by `orderId` → idempotent upsert).

**`orders`** — owns the lifecycle. `OrderAggregate` (client-supplied `orderId` as aggregate id → duplicate creates rejected by the platform; decisions accepted only while PENDING → exactly one decision, no status regression). `OrderSaga` orchestrates **reserve → charge → confirm** with compensation (release on insufficient funds). `OrderProjector`/`Projection` and `StatsProjector`/`Projection` serve order and stats views.

**`edge`** — stateless gateway: `ApiInvoker` (`@Invoker`) + `ApiController` (REST), no DB, no aggregates.

### How the invariants are met
- **No oversell / no double-spend:** the platform serializes commands per aggregate id, so the `ProductAggregate`/`CustomerAggregate` consistency boundaries make the races deterministic — exactly K confirm, balance never negative.
- **Idempotent orders:** duplicate `orderId` → `AggregateInitializedError`, caught at the edge and returned as a 202 replay; the single `OrderCreatedEvent` drives the saga once.
- **Exactly-once notifications & stats:** single-active ordered consumers + JDBC dedupe store + notification rows keyed by `orderId`.
- **Compensation:** `ChargeFailedEvent` → saga releases the reservation, then rejects — no residual effect.
- **Each saga step is its own checkpointed event handler**, so a mid-flow restart resumes without re-issuing applied commands.
- **Durability:** all business state lives in Postgres (read models) and the Evento event store; consumer checkpoints/saga state use the pre-wired JDBC state store. I verified an order's CONFIRMED state, stock, balance, and notifications all survive a full restart, and new orders process correctly afterward.
